book.title: Hebrews
book.titleOfficial: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE

chapter.summary: The Son is in the express image of the person of the Father—Christ is the Only Begotten Son and thus above the angels.

verses.text: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,

footNotes.text: GR in many locations and various ways.

verses.text: Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;

footNotes.text: TG Godhead; Jesus Christ, Divine Sonship; Jesus Christ, Jehovah.
Matt. 21:38 (33–46). TG Jesus Christ, Relationships with the Father.

verses.text: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;

footNotes.text: TG God, Body of, Corporeal Nature.

verses.text: Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?

footNotes.text: Heb. 5:5. TG Jesus Christ, Divine Sonship.

verses.text: And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.

footNotes.text: JST Heb. 1:6–7 … And let all the angels of God worship him, who maketh his ministers as a flame of fire. And of the angels he saith, Angels are ministering spirits.

verses.text: And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.

footNotes.text: TG Kingdom of God, in Heaven.

verses.text: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands:
They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment;
And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?
Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
